short: Diffusion EEG decoder (M06) standard: Diff-E lineage, no ablation, not smaller. Online use (M13) standard: one patient, 20 trials. M12: Table I overall row disagrees with class rows.
position: The paper [@ko2025lightweight] changes the decoder (M06) and runs it online with one person with aphasia (M13). M06 is standard: the design belongs to the Diff-E lineage, which already classified without reverse sampling [@kim2023diffe; @kim2024ensemble; @park2025viseme], and at 14.11 M parameters the network is larger than Diff-E, not lighter (§II-D.3). M13 is standard: online decoding departs from the offline default (112 of 167 imagined-speech EEG studies, pattern match, Appendix), but an earlier online study tested 20 participants over two sessions [@wu2024adaptive] against one participant and 20 trials here. The main problem is M12: the All row of Table I (65% top-1, 70% top-2) does not follow from its class rows. Without baseline or ablation (§III), what diffusion adds is untested. What holds is a working clinical pipeline: about 30 minutes of calibration, about 20 seconds of fitting (§III-A).
